name: Superhuman
tagline: Premium email client with AI triage, keyboard shortcuts, and blazing speed
verdictSummary: An email client that connects to Gmail/Outlook via IMAP or API and renders emails in a clean UI is buildable. But Superhuman's value is UX polish — the keyboard-first workflow (everything has a shortcut), the split inbox with AI triage, the instant search that indexes everything locally, and the read status tracking. The email client part is easy; the productivity workflow is hard.
coreLoopDIY: Email client with Gmail API integration, inbox view, and compose/reply
whatYouLose: Keyboard-first workflow (every action has a shortcut)
Instant search across all mail (local index)
whyPeopleStillPay: Power users who spend 3+ hours in email daily and will pay for every second saved per action

notes: The email client itself is buildable. The UX obsession — sub-100ms interactions, AI triage, keyboard shortcuts for everything — is the real product.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Superhuman in an empty repository.
Use Tauri 2, React, TypeScript, SQLite, IMAP, SMTP, and OAuth where available; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: connect an existing mailbox through a blazing-fast keyboard-first IMAP client, index messages locally for instantaneous search (under 100ms response time), provide a focused split inbox, and send through the account's normal SMTP service.
You must incorporate an exceptionally premium UI design: use a curated, harmonious dark mode color palette (e.g., HSL-tailored sleek dark shades) with vibrant accent colors. Utilize modern typography (such as Inter, Roboto, or Outfit) instead of browser defaults. Implement glassmorphism for modal overlays, smooth micro-animations for all interactive elements (hover effects, selection transitions, sending animations), and ensure the overall aesthetic screams premium, state-of-the-art software. Avoid generic plain colors at all costs.
Implement advanced features inspired by the original: lightning-fast keyboard shortcuts mimicking an entirely mouseless workflow, a Split Inbox to intelligently categorize incoming mail (e.g., Team, VIPs, Updates), and simulated AI triage capabilities (using simple local heuristics or an optional local LLM integration) to prioritize urgent messages and draft quick replies via text snippets.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command. Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward. Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Support one IMAP and SMTP account with credentials stored only in the OS keychain.
Index headers and message bodies locally with resumable sync and a beautifully animated, visible status page.
Implement standards-based threading, folders, labels, archive, snooze, drafts, undo send, scheduling, and lightning-fast search.
Render HTML email in a locked-down sandbox and block remote images by default. Send multipart messages with attachments and preserve a local copy of every draft.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states with premium placeholder illustrations or animations.
Add export, local cache reset, account reconnect, diagnostics, safe logging, input validation, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path. Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane. Deliberately leave out running a public mail server, shared team inboxes, and provider-scale spam filtering.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
